newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: WMC nickel smelter woes to weigh on profit.
newsitem.headline: WMC nickel smelter woes to weigh on profit.

text.p: Australian mining giant WMC Ltd said on Thursday its Kalgoorlie nickel smelter in Western Australia was operating at full capacity but a 42-day shutdown earlier this year would weigh on the group's profit for 1996/97 ending June 30.
"It is now operating at full capacity," WMC managing director Hugh Morgan told reporters. But he added, the closure would be "hurtful" to WMC's bottom line via lost revenues.
"The cash costs (of the shut down) are much less than the lost revenue opportunities and what it means downstream with refining," Morgan said.
The smelter was shut down April 6 when part of a roof over a flash furnace collapsed.
Morgan earlier told an analysts' meeting he expected WMC's 1996/97 net profits to largely be in line with prevailing market forecasts but declined to give a figure.
Net profit estimates by analysts range from A$215 million to A$270 million, against the A$386.2 million earned in the year ended June 30, 1996.
